notes:
- Currently arriving is square and even: a 1:1 cover, two reserved title lines, and the airing/upcoming colour groups kept.
- The profile arranges itself from its own bar: the layout palette is in the app bar, the two-up characters are centred pairs, and all fifty pinned characters are fetched.
- The hero shows the banner and searches the web: the backdrop crossfades from poster to banner, Search the web joins the action capsule, and Open on AniList no longer fails silently.
- A studio reads two ways: year shelves or one packed wall, chosen from the page's bar.
- A creator's page introduces them properly: the staff hero leads with occupations and the native name, filmographies gain All/Anime/Manga chips, AniList moved onto the hero, and two Stats charts lost their phone and stopwatch glyphs.
- The library bar carries its number: an animated count badge beside the name and the trophy in a soft capsule.
- Smaller fixes: the text-size preview no longer reflows per tick; full screen re-asserts on every resume, keeps the status bar's height above the top bar, and the cover viewer hides the bars in its own window.
- Full screen, when you want it: Appearance hides the status and navigation bars on request, an edge swipe brings them back, and the root keeps cutout and breathing room so a header never sits on the glass. Off by default.
- Five ways to move, all of them visible: Snappy and Floaty join Instant, Smooth and Chill, the picker wraps so no style hides off the edge, and the sample plays the chosen style's own spring with the overshoot shown as a pulse - tap to replay.
- Your own font, at your own size: Settings > Type & reading scales every text style from 85% to 130% and imports any .ttf or .otf, copied into the app and validated so the choice is permanent.
- Long titles scroll instead of cutting: a title too wide for its row rests, then scrolls and repeats; the speed is a setting with a live sample, and Instant turns it off.
- The tier board waits for your list: tapping Tiers from a cold start built the board before the viewer query answered and could rank the demo fixture into the reader's own DataStore. It now waits, and fails the way the Library page does.
- A number is not an identity: anime and manga share AniList ids, and the favourites chip, merged library grid, quick-add state, theme-song cache, LiveChart poster cache and progress-wave entrance all crossed that line. Each carries its namespace now.
- Signing in survives the browser trip: a callback that arrives after the process was killed is handled, a replayed one is ignored, and a cancelled save no longer leaves an unverified token behind.
- An update download cannot start twice: a rotation mid-download re-ran the update check and could open a second stream into the same part file. Checks are refused while a transfer runs, and a short body is a dropped connection that resumes.
- The dashboard stops showing the previous profile: a library download could publish its older overview over a fresh one. The state is rebuilt from whoever is current, and the invalidation counters are atomic.
- Widgets forget an account that signed out: signed-out tiles kept the old handle and titles indefinitely. They are emptied on sign-out, cover fetches are bounded, and the store is excluded from backup and transfer.
- Undo puts back the title it named: hiding two entries quickly made the first Undo restore the second, and a restore could re-hide an entry already brought back. The snackbar carries its own entry and the store takes the intended state.
- The hold button moves like one control: its colour chased a per-frame target, the fill re-laid-out per frame, and its press spring differed from every other control. The hidden-anime section's four literal springs are the shared size token.
- The bar's pages move on the bar's spring: the tier page uses the tab spring now, the bar keeps its real tab while it leaves, the cover viewer's exit settles inside its window, and the counter, calendar and Read more expansions are tokenized.
- Four palettes get their surfaces back: Sakura, Matcha, Jupiter and Sunset now carry the app's neutral ladder, and the bar's clearance is its real 86dp.
- Smaller fixes: server errors inside GraphQL errors, blank titles, two tap targets under 48dp, a poster's spoken name, markdown links and centred images, the studio title count, the tier export bitmap cap, and the person sheet's appearances scroll.
- Ani-chan can be renamed, and stamped: the Name, stamp and size card renames the speaker, swaps the badge glyph for any character from a small palette or the keyboard, and offers a compact pill with just the line and the heart.
- The pill can type: Line style offers typewriter, word-by-word and fade-up text, all off by default, with a live sample that plays the real speed.
- Updates is its own page: the updater and What's new moved off About onto a shelf page of their own.
- More dark lines, and a faster draw: fifty new DARK jokes, and the tone filter is computed once per switch combination instead of on every draw.\n- The inbox can answer: a reply box under an open message with Public/Private choice, private by default, addressed to the other party and naming them in the confirmation.\n- Your profile, arranged how you read it: the header palette button opens an editor to reorder blocks, hide and unhide them, switch favourite characters to a two-column grid, and reset - stored on the device, with new blocks appended rather than hidden.
- The export is yours to style: show or hide the title, size it S/M/L, pick Sans/Serif/Mono, with a live name sample and an honest pixel-size estimate.
- Arriving is two groups, one card: Airing now and Upcoming share one card at one cover height and are told apart by background colour.
- Genres fold away: the filter sheet's Genre block collapses from its own header with the shared motion tokens.
- Hidden sequels show their faces: hidden rows draw the real poster over its tinted placeholder.
- The press lands sooner and the pill arrives quicker: a stiffer press-in spring and the fast offset token on the joke pill.
- Twenty more ways it ended: the dark pool grew by twenty lines in its own voice.
